title: ClusterRoles & ClusterRoleBindings 🌍
description: Extend RBAC beyond namespaces with cluster‑scoped permissions.

slides.title: When Roles Aren’t Enough 🌐
slides.content:
# Some resources have no namespace

Nodes, PersistentVolumes, Namespaces themselves, and some APIs (like `certificates.k8s.io`) are **cluster‑scoped**. A Role (namespaced) cannot grant access to them.

**ClusterRoles** work like Roles but can cover:
- Cluster‑scoped resources
- Non‑resource endpoints (e.g., `/healthz`)
- Resources in all namespaces at once

slides.title: ClusterRole YAML 📝
slides.content:
## A cluster‑wide Node reader

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: node-reader
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["nodes"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
```

No namespace is needed.

quizData.question: Which resource is cluster‑scoped and requires a ClusterRole?
quizData.explanation: Nodes are not namespaced; they need a ClusterRole.

slides.title: ClusterRoleBinding 🔗
slides.content:
## Bind the ClusterRole globally

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: read-nodes
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: node-inspector
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: node-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

Now that ServiceAccount can see all nodes cluster‑wide.

slides.title: Using ClusterRole with RoleBinding 🧩
slides.content:
## Reuse ClusterRoles in a namespace

You can bind a ClusterRole to a **RoleBinding** (not ClusterRoleBinding). Then the permissions are scoped to that namespace only.

Example: the built‑in `view` ClusterRole lets you read most objects. You can bind it to a user only in the `dev` namespace:
```yaml
kind: RoleBinding
name: dev-view
namespace: dev
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: alice
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

Alice can view everything in `dev`, but nowhere else.

quizData.question: If you bind a ClusterRole via a RoleBinding, where does the permission apply?

options.text: Only in the namespace of the RoleBinding

quizData.explanation: A RoleBinding restricts the scope to its own namespace, even if the role is a ClusterRole.

slides.title: Built‑in ClusterRoles 👑
slides.content:
## Kubernetes ships with handy defaults

- **cluster‑admin** – full control.
- **admin** – full control in a namespace (including RBAC).
- **edit** – modify most objects, but not RBAC or quotas.
- **view** – read‑only access to most objects.

Use `kubectl get clusterroles` to see them. Avoid reinventing the wheel for common patterns.

slides.title: Check Built‑in ClusterRoles
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl get clusterroles
kubectl describe clusterrole view

slides.title: Aggregated ClusterRoles 🧬
slides.content:
## Build larger roles from smaller ones

You can use labels to combine ClusterRoles. Example:
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: combined-role
aggregationRule:
  clusterRoleSelectors:
  - matchLabels:
      rbac.example.com/aggregate-to-combined: "true"
rules: []  # rules are dynamically merged
```

Other ClusterRoles with matching label will have their rules added automatically. Handy for extending built‑in roles.

quizData.question: What does an aggregated ClusterRole do?

options.text: Merges rules from other ClusterRoles matching a label

quizData.explanation: Aggregation allows dynamic rule composition based on labels.
